Photic

An interactive demo of our underwater path tracer. Every image below is a real render.

The tank

Start with plain Homework 3 (no water), then switch the medium on and change what's in it. Absorption reddens out with depth, particulates scatter and flatten contrast, and the phase function decides which way the light goes.

absorption sigma_a0.35 0.05 0.015
particulates sigma_s0.15
depth scalex4
optical depth1.2
Drag a slider and the image swaps to the matching render.

Why forward scattering matters

The scattering toggle picks a Henyey-Greenstein phase function. Drag g to see the whole range: back-scattering, isotropic, and the tight forward lobe of real water.

forward is to the right
asymmetry   g = 0.90
p(cos) = (1 - g^2) / 4pi(1 + g^2 - 2g cos)^1.5
mean scatter cosine = g

Measured against the physics

We fit the attenuation coefficient Kd off the renders and compare to the naive single-scattering prediction. The gap is the multiple scattering the whole project is about.

What's under the hood

Homogeneous medium

Bounded water volume auto-fit to any HW3 scene; analytic free-flight distance sampling, no ray marching.

Per-channel absorption

RGB Beer-Lambert extinction; red dies fast, blue survives, which is the color of depth.

Particulate scattering

Turbidity sets sigma_s; more particulates means more in-scatter and softer contrast.

Henyey-Greenstein

Importance-sampled phase function with adjustable g; the pdf equals the phase value, so it cancels cleanly.

Multiple scattering

Next-event estimation plus a Russian-roulette recursive continuation, so extra bounces emerge on their own.

Measurement and convergence

Fits Kd per channel and studies noise vs samples across optical depth, straight off the rendered PNGs.
